hero.title: MIDDAY NEWS & GLOBAL UPDATE
hero.subtitle: World affairs, elections, public health and the issues shaping people's lives

summary: Today's bulletin examines the US midterm-election debate over household costs, tensions between Canada and Washington, UK retail figures, protests in Paris, Typhoon Champi's impact in Taiwan, the Ebola response, and Nigeria's preparations for the 2027 elections. Developing claims should be checked against the linked reporting and official updates.
breaking: US midterm elections are scheduled for 3 November 2026, with the cost of living a major campaign issue.
Nigeria's 2027 campaign season is taking shape as parties and opposition groups debate their strategies.
Health authorities continue surveillance and contact tracing following Nigeria's reported imported Ebola case.

featured.title: Nigeria 2027: Ask the Candidates for Answers, Not Just Promises
featured.summary: RadiantWaves Media invites presidential aspirants and their representatives to participate in fair, evidence-led interviews and submit written responses on the economy, security, electricity, public spending and measurable results.

topStories.title: USA: Cost of Living Looms Over Midterm Elections
topStories.summary: Rising household costs are a political vulnerability for President Donald Trump and Republican candidates ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Reuters reports that a Reuters/Ipsos poll found many respondents blamed Trump's policies for prices rising faster than their earnings. Poll findings reflect public opinion and do not establish that government policy alone caused price increases.

topStories.title: Canada: Carney Rejects US Election-Interference Allegations
topStories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has rejected US allegations that Canadian politicians are interfering in American midterm elections. The dispute adds to wider tensions over trade and tariffs. The allegations remain contested.

topStories.title: UK: Retail Sales Volumes Fell in September
topStories.summary: Official figures show retail sales volumes in Great Britain fell by 0.4% in September after rising in August. Sales volumes remained above their level a year earlier, indicating a mixed consumer picture rather than a uniform collapse in spending.
topStories.imageAlt: High street retail shops in the United Kingdom

topStories.title: France: Paris Prepares for Further Demonstrations
topStories.summary: Businesses in parts of Paris have been boarding up shopfronts ahead of further demonstrations following violence during earlier protests. Authorities face the challenge of protecting residents and businesses while respecting peaceful protest. The scale of any further unrest remains developing news.

topStories.title: Taiwan: Typhoon Champi Leaves One Dead and Hundreds Injured
topStories.summary: Channel NewsAsia reported that Typhoon Champi left one person dead and 527 injured in Taiwan. The storm caused disruption, including power interruptions and transport impacts. Follow local authorities for current safety guidance and updated figures.
topStories.imageAlt: Typhoon conditions and storm damage in Taiwan

topStories.title: Africa: Nigeria Continues Ebola Response and Contact Tracing
topStories.summary: Nigerian authorities reported an imported Ebola case in Abuja and initiated public-health measures, including isolation and contact tracing. Reported genetic similarity between viruses identified in Nigeria and Kenya does not by itself prove that the patients met or that one directly infected the other. Follow official health updates for confirmed information.
topStories.imageAlt: Public health response and disease surveillance

topStories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Campaign Activity Reported in Kaduna
topStories.summary: Reports said President Bola Tinubu's re-election campaign activity was scheduled to begin in Kaduna on 24 October. Voters will want evidence and clear plans on living costs, insecurity, electricity, jobs and public spending. Confirm event details with the campaign and reputable reporting before updating this story.

topStories.title: Nigeria: Opposition Unity Talks Face Difficult Choices
topStories.summary: Reporting describes discussions among opposition figures and groups about a possible common presidential candidate for 2027, including camps associated with Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. Differences over leadership, party platforms and candidate selection remain obstacles. A unified ticket is not guaranteed.
topStories.imageAlt: Political discussions ahead of Nigeria's 2027 election

topStories.title: Global Economy: Energy Prices and Markets Remain Sensitive to Geopolitical Risks
topStories.summary: Geopolitical tensions, trade disputes and uncertainty over energy supplies can influence oil prices and financial markets, with possible effects on transport, food distribution and inflation. Market movements have multiple causes and should not be attributed to a single event without evidence.
topStories.imageAlt: Global financial markets and energy prices

electionWatch.summary: US midterm elections are scheduled for 3 November. Voters will choose members of Congress and decide a range of state and local contests.

The reported 2027 calendar lists presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January and governorship and State House of Assembly elections for 6 February. Check INEC's current official timetable before publication or updating these dates.
General elections have been planned for 22 December 2026. Given the country's transitional political context, monitor the National Elections Commission for any change to the timetable.

publicInterestFeature.title: 2027 Presidential Questions: Where Are the Answers?
publicInterestFeature.eyebrow: RADIANTWAVES MEDIA — PUBLIC INTEREST INTERVIEW & RIGHT-OF-REPLY INITIATIVE
publicInterestFeature.intro: As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, RadiantWaves Media Nigeria Ltd invites declared and prospective presidential aspirants, candidates, campaign organisations and authorised representatives to share their plans, answer public-interest questions and provide evidence that voters can examine.
publicInterestFeature.purpose: Our aim is to help the public compare policies, records and measurable commitments fairly. We welcome interview requests, written opinions, policy documents and evidence-based responses from candidates across political parties.
publicInterestFeature.questionsHeading: Core questions for every participating aspirant

questions.question: Cost of Living and the Economy
questions.detail: What practical steps would you take to address inflation, food prices, jobs, wages and household purchasing power? What targets and timelines would you publish?

questions.question: Fuel, Energy and Electricity
questions.detail: What is your plan for fuel affordability, energy security and reliable electricity? How would you fund the plan and measure progress?

questions.question: Security and Public Safety
questions.detail: How would your administration improve security, protect communities and strengthen accountability for the use of security resources?

questions.question: Public Spending and Accountability
questions.detail: How would you make public contracts, budgets, borrowing and government spending more transparent, and how would citizens track delivery?

questions.question: Record in Public Office
questions.detail: What verifiable results from your previous public service or leadership experience demonstrate your ability to deliver the promises you are making?

questions.question: Jobs, Education and Health
questions.detail: What measurable commitments would you make on employment, skills, schools and access to healthcare, and how would you report progress?

questions.question: First 100 Days and First Year
questions.detail: What three priorities would you pursue first, what would they cost, and what independent evidence would show whether they had worked?

participation.invitation: Presidential aspirants and authorised representatives are invited to request a journalistic interview or submit a written response or opinion article addressing these questions.
submissionGuidance: Identify the candidate and the authorised person submitting the response.
Provide a short biography and the candidate's current political role or declared status.
Answer the questions directly and include supporting documents, data or official links where available.
State clearly whether claims are proposals, targets, completed actions or allegations.
Provide contact details for verification and follow-up.
participation.readerParticipation: Readers may suggest additional public-interest questions for consideration. Questions should be relevant, fair and applicable consistently to participating candidates.

editorialStandards: RadiantWaves will seek to apply the same core questions and comparable standards to participating candidates, while allowing relevant follow-up questions.
Claims and documents will be checked as far as reasonably possible against reliable sources and independent evidence.
A candidate's statement will be identified as that candidate's position and will not automatically be presented as an established fact.
Candidates will have a reasonable opportunity to respond to material, relevant allegations before publication where practicable.
Participation, non-participation or a delayed response will not by itself be treated as proof of wrongdoing.
Publication decisions remain subject to verification, editorial judgement, available space and applicable law. An invitation does not guarantee publication.
publicInterestFeature.closing: The public deserves more than slogans. We invite candidates to explain their plans, show their evidence and be judged fairly by the electorate.
publicInterestFeature.imageAlt: RadiantWaves Media public-interest presidential interview initiative

thoughtForToday.title: RadiantWaves Thought for Today
thoughtForToday.text: Democracy grows stronger when leaders answer for their decisions and citizens judge them by evidence, not promises.

todaysBigQuestion.title: Today's Big Question
todaysBigQuestion.text: With elections approaching in Nigeria and the United States, what should matter most to voters: economic results, security, or the integrity and accountability of political leaders?
todaysBigQuestion.prompt: Share your views respectfully. Healthy debate begins with facts.
